instruction: Save the Rotary Embeddings blog post from the other tab to your bookmarks bar.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully bookmarked the active tab (Illustrated Transformer) to bookmarks bar using Ctrl+D, changed folder to Bookmarks bar, and toggled bar visibility with Ctrl+Shift+B. Completed in 6 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can switch tabs, use Ctrl+D to bookmark, select bookmark folder, toggle bookmarks bar visibility
metadata.task_rationale: Tests same bookmarking capability but requires switching to the non-active tab first, adding a tab navigation step
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the Rotary Embeddings tab (not currently active) and bookmarking it to the bookmarks bar. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks bookmarks bar contains the target URL.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_bookmarks) correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file and returns the roots dict containing bookmark_bar data
Metric (is_expected_bookmarks) correctly handles 'bookmark_bar_websites_urls' rule type, extracting URLs from bookmark_bar children
Expected URL (https://blog.eleuther.ai/rotary-embeddings/) correctly matches the Rotary Embeddings blog post specified in the instruction
Postconfig correctly kills and restarts Chrome to ensure bookmarks are persisted to disk before the getter reads them
get_rule returns config['rules'] directly, so metric receives the rules dict correctly as the 'rule' parameter

Minor concern: metric uses strict set equality (set(actual) == set(expected)) rather than subset check — if pre-existing bookmarks exist in the bar, verification would incorrectly fail. In a clean OSWorld environment this is unlikely but makes the evaluator slightly fragile
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using set(rule['urls']).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls)) instead of strict set equality, to allow pre-existing bookmarks in the bar without causing false negatives
